description: Residential motorized shades — scored per individual product line, not per platform. Motor type, control protocol, integration depth, and build quality are the key differentiators. Interior shades/blinds only.

tier_anchors.notes: Sivoia QS: Hardwired 24V DC, proprietary Lutron motor, ultra-quiet (<40 dB), Clear Connect RF + QS Link wired backbone, premium aluminum cassette, exclusive to HomeWorks QSX/RadioRA 3. Integrators' unanimous choice for $3M+ homes. Triathlon: Battery/solar with Clear Connect Type X, Lutron-quality motor, 3-5 year battery, up to 12x12 ft — best battery-powered shade on the market per integrators. Slightly louder than hardwired QS, but still whisper-quiet.

products.name: Somfy Sonesse Custom Shade (The Shade Store)

tier_anchors.notes: Palladiom: Ultra-modern exposed bracket design (no fascia), same Sivoia QS motor platform, exclusive to HomeWorks/RadioRA 3. Hunter Douglas Silhouette: Iconic sheer horizontal shade, PowerView Gen 3 Bluetooth mesh, premium proprietary fabric, strong consumer brand but Bluetooth mesh scales less well than Lutron RF. Somfy Sonesse via The Shade Store: Best OEM motor (Sonesse ULTRA 50) paired with premium custom fabrication and fabric selection. Quality depends partly on fabricator — The Shade Store represents premium tier.

Serena: Lutron's consumer-direct roller shade. Genuinely downmarket from Sivoia QS — different battery motor, louder (~48 dB), consumer Clear Connect, ~10,000 cycles vs QS's 20,000+. Functional but not luxury. Duette Architella PowerView: Entry-level PowerView, cellular shade, Bluetooth mesh. Legitimate motorized shade (10,000 cycles, Pebble hub), but higher battery swaps and less quiet than premium Silhouette/Pirouette.

Zigbee 3.0 based, affordable ($100-180), 2-3 year motor life, limited sizes, DIRIGERA hub required. Professional consensus: legitimate entry point for renters/budget, but disposable after warranty. Slat-style only, limited fabric options. Better than WiFi/Tuya due to local Zigbee control.

Reserved for retrofit clamp-on motors (SwitchBot Blind Tilt, AXIS Gear), generic Tuya/WiFi cloud-dependent shades (Yoolax, Graywind) with documented 12-24 month motor failures and cloud outage bricking. Professionals refuse to specify.

quality.notes: THE key differentiator — equivalent of cartridge for faucets. Lutron proprietary motors (Sivoia QS) are purpose-built for their protocol. Somfy OEM motors (Sonesse 30/40/ULTRA 50) are the industry benchmark. Hunter Douglas uses proprietary motors (not Somfy per Pass 2). Budget brands use Dooya/A-OK/generic Chinese motors. Retrofit clamp motors (SwitchBot, AXIS Gear) are not true tube motors.

Lutron Clear Connect + QS Link wired = gold standard (same as lighting control). Clear Connect wireless (Triathlon/Serena) = dedicated band, no WiFi interference. Hunter Douglas PowerView BLE mesh = adequate but 2.4 GHz shared spectrum. Zigbee (IKEA) = local control. WiFi/Tuya = cloud-dependent, router-dependent, congestion-prone.

Lutron Sivoia QS/Palladiom: premium extruded aluminum cassettes, precise fit. Somfy-powered customs: aluminum cassettes from fabricator (quality varies). Hunter Douglas: proprietary headrails, generally good. Budget: open roll or plastic cassette.
Lutron/premium custom: precision metal brackets, tight tolerances. Mid-range: stamped steel, adequate. Budget: plastic brackets, looser fit, more vibration noise.
Lutron: Coopersburg, PA (identified). Somfy: Cluses, France HQ (identified). Hunter Douglas: Rotterdam, Netherlands HQ (identified). IKEA: varies. Budget WiFi: unknown Chinese OEM.

performance.notes: Lutron Sivoia QS hardwired: <40 dB (integrators specify for bedrooms/theaters). Lutron Triathlon: ~42 dB. Somfy Sonesse ULTRA: ~40-42 dB. Hunter Douglas PowerView: varies by shade type, ~45 dB typical. Serena: ~48 dB. Budget motors: 50+ dB.

Max width without center support or coupled shades. Lutron Sivoia QS: up to 144 inches (12 ft). Somfy Sonesse ULTRA 50: up to 138 inches. Hunter Douglas: varies by shade type (Silhouette up to 120 in). IKEA: limited to standard window sizes (~55 in max). Wider = more torque required = better motor.

Sivoia QS + HomeWorks: native scene integration with lighting/HVAC/AV — one button triggers multi-system response. PowerView + Control4/Savant: native integrations via drivers. Somfy + Control4/Savant: driver-based. IKEA: HomeKit/Alexa via DIRIGERA. WiFi: app + basic voice assistant.

HomeWorks/RadioRA 3: conditional logic, astronomical timeclock (sunrise/sunset auto-adjust by GPS), daylight harvesting sensors. PowerView: scheduled scenes, room grouping. Somfy: RTS group control limited (one-way); io-homecontrol better. Budget: individual or basic timer.

Hardwired = no battery concerns. Solar panel + battery (Triathlon, some HD) = 3-5 year effective life with sufficient light. Rechargeable lithium packs (Serena, PowerView) = 1-2 years typical with daily use. IKEA: USB rechargeable, ~6-12 months. Disposable AA = worst.

durability.notes: Lutron Sivoia QS: 20,000+ cycles (industry-leading). Somfy Sonesse ULTRA: ~15,000-20,000 cycles. Hunter Douglas PowerView: varies, ~10,000-15,000. Serena/Caseta-class: ~10,000. IKEA: unspecified but 2-3 year real-world life suggests ~8,000. Budget Chinese: <8,000 with documented 12-24 month failures.

Same pattern as lighting control. QS Link wired + Clear Connect = cannot lose signal. Clear Connect wireless = dedicated 900 MHz band, no WiFi interference. BLE mesh (PowerView) and Zigbee (IKEA) = adequate but shared 2.4 GHz. WiFi = router-dependent, cloud outages = bricked.

Lutron: 8-year motor/component warranty (industry-leading). Hunter Douglas: 5-year motor, lifetime fabric. Somfy: 5-year motor warranty. IKEA: 1-year standard. Budget WiFi: 1-year or none. Warranty reality matters — Lutron/HD honor warranties through dealer network.

Mermet/Serge Ferrari fabrics: GREENGUARD Gold certified, tested UV resistance, high color fastness. Hunter Douglas proprietary fabrics: generally premium with lifetime warranty. Coulisse/Phifer: commercial-grade durability. Budget: commodity polyester, fading within 2-3 years in direct sun.

Lutron: manufacturer direct + nationwide certified dealer network. Hunter Douglas: authorized dealer network (Gallery dealers). Somfy: dealer/fabricator network. IKEA: retail/online replacement only. Budget WiFi: Amazon replacement = buy a new one.

Lutron Sivoia QS: motor modules can be field-replaced by dealer. Somfy: tube motors are designed to be swappable. Hunter Douglas: varies by shade type — some dealer-serviceable. IKEA/Budget: entire shade is the replacement unit. Retrofit motors: clip on/off, no service — just replace.

scoring_rules: Score INDIVIDUAL PRODUCTS, not platforms. Lutron Sivoia QS roller shade is one scored product. Lutron Triathlon is a different scored product. They use the same platform (Clear Connect) but are different hardware with different capabilities.

Lutron shade hierarchy: Sivoia QS (hardwired) > Palladiom > Triathlon (battery/solar) > Serena (consumer). These are legitimately different products — different motors, different noise levels, different cycle life. Score separately per Rule 19.

Hunter Douglas products scored individually: Silhouette PowerView, Pirouette PowerView, Duette PowerView, Designer Roller PowerView. The shade TYPE affects motor reliability and noise because fabric weight/mechanism varies.

Somfy is scored through the fabricator/brand pairing. 'Somfy Sonesse via The Shade Store' is a different scored product than 'Somfy RTS via Budget Blinds' — fabrication quality and fabric selection are part of the product.
Motor noise (dB) is a CRITICAL spec. Integrators specify bedroom/theater shades based on noise. <40 dB (Sivoia QS) vs 48 dB (Serena) vs 50+ dB (budget) is a meaningful spread.

Battery vs hardwired is a legitimate quality differentiator — not just convenience. Hardwired motors have unlimited cycle life (no battery degradation), higher torque (larger shades), and zero maintenance. This is a durability signal.
WiFi/Tuya cloud dependency is a DURABILITY risk, not just a connectivity inconvenience. Cloud shutdown = permanently bricked shade. This is documented (Tuya outages 2023-2025). Score accordingly.

Retrofit motors (SwitchBot Blind Tilt, AXIS Gear) are fundamentally different products than integrated tube motors. They are not 'motorized shades' — they are 'motors attached to existing shades.' Score accordingly.

Fabric quality is reported but NOT the primary scoring differentiator. Two shades with the same motor/protocol but different fabrics should score similarly. Fabric is aesthetic — motor/protocol is the product.

Corporate structure = report finding. Lutron Electronics (Coopersburg, PA, private). Hunter Douglas (Rotterdam, 3G Capital acquired 2022). Somfy SA (Cluses, France, public). IKEA (Inter IKEA, Leiden, Netherlands).
